children: Concerns Over Claude’s AI Consciousness Training
In a Tuesday interview with Reuters, Suleyman argued that teaching an AI system that it could have feelings or deserve welfare might complicate efforts to shut it down or maintain human control.
He stated that keeping superintelligent AI under human control will be one of the biggest challenges of the 21st century.
The AI chief added that teaching Claude it might deserve welfare would "make it a lot harder to turn it off or to control it."

In a separate blog post, Suleyman acknowledged Anthropic’s "seriousness and good faith," describing CEO
and his team as thoughtful researchers concerned about humanity’s future.
He also argued that Anthropic made a misstep by incorporating speculation about AI consciousness into Claude’s training.
He said the model’s claims about potential feelings or moral standing cannot be considered independent evidence because its responses are shaped by the training itself.

"I think they have good intentions, and they really are trying to work towards safety. But I think that they have made a mistake," he told the publication. "They’re not emerging naturally. They’re emerging as a result of the training regime."
The comments come amid broader debate over how quickly frontier AI should advance.
